title: Grok: allow write roles
lead: *Proposed:* let the grok adapter run write roles, for `grok` and `grok-local`. The owner lifted the earlier ban on 2026-11-07 for all grok. It needs an adj record that supersedes the S72 ruling; the owner records it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
- S72 refuses a write role because headless grok refuses every write under `dontAsk` and `acceptEdits` (probes 10 to 12), and the owner had ruled out `bypassPermissions` and `--always-approve` (`CHANGELOG.md`, S72 entry).
- The adapter refuses a write role at `internal/agent/grok/grok.go:61-62`, and `matrixUse` still says "used as grok" for write rows (`internal/daemon/matrix.go:75-78`).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- A write role on grok builds a command with the permission mode the owner picks and runs in the slice worktree; a read-only role is unchanged.
- The same holds for `grok-local`.
- `ork roles matrix` no longer marks a grok write row as skipped.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. The owner records the adj decision first (supersede the S72 ruling; which flag).
2. Probe on the owner's machine: one write role under the chosen mode, headless, in a scratch worktree. Record the command and result.
3. Remove the refusal, pass the flag, keep the S280 cancel handling, and update `matrixUse` and the brief.
4. Update the docs.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- The adj record is decided and cited.
- The probe result is in the handoff note.
- `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .`, `slicer check`, `adj lint`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: - Branch and worktree per AGENTS.md; no commit until the owner approves.
